nodes.text: M-morning. Or whatever it is by now — the pond keeps its own clock and I keep the pond's.

choices.text: Where does the water go, downriver?
Why ring the bell at dawn?

nodes.text: Down to *Saltmere*, in the end — salt flats, grey gulls, boats with eyes painted on them. I walked up from there when I was small enough to count my ribs. One day I'll pole somebody the whole way back down, when the river and I have saved up the nerve between us. The water remembers the way. Rivers don't forget anything, they just c-carry it downstream.

So the pond knows I'm here. So *Garton* knows I'm here — he'd never ask, but his window faces the water and the bell saves him the walk. And... the wind rings it sometimes on its own. I let it. Everything likes to say good morning.
Trout, mostly — the pond's generous if you're p-patient. Rod's for sale too, if you'd rather argue with the fish yourself.
You too. Mind the reeds if you swim — they're friendlier than they look, but they *are* clingy.
